faithfulness.text: It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his mercies don’t fail. They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness.
faithfulness.question: Where have you seen a mercy that was new this morning?

faithfulness.text: Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
faithfulness.question: What are you trusting God for that you cannot yet see?

kingdom.text: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
kingdom.question: What would seeking his kingdom first look like tomorrow?

kingdom.text: Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. Your dominion endures throughout all generations. Yahweh is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.
kingdom.question: Which earthly power feels largest to you right now, and how does this verse resize it?

courage.text: Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go.
courage.question: Where do you most need courage this week?

courage.text: Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
courage.question: What would you attempt if you were sure God was holding you up?

mercy.text: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
mercy.question: Which of the three, justice, mercy, or humility, is hardest for you today?

mercy.text: Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful.
mercy.question: Who needs mercy from you that they have not earned?

word.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
word.question: What is the next step this lamp is lighting for you?

word.text: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.
word.question: What have you been treating as permanent that is really grass?

calling.text: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”
calling.question: What might you need to leave on the shore in order to follow?

calling.text: You didn’t choose me, but I chose you, and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.
calling.question: How does being chosen first change how you see your work?

church.text: See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!
church.question: Who in your church could you move toward this week?

church.text: so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.
church.question: Whom do you belong to, and who belongs to you?

mission.text: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”
mission.question: Where might God be asking, "Whom shall I send?" in your own neighbourhood?

mission.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.
mission.question: Where is your Jerusalem, the place nearest to hand?

worship.text: Oh come, let’s worship and bow down. Let’s kneel before Yahweh, our Maker,
worship.question: When did you last stop and simply kneel?

worship.text: God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.
worship.question: What would worship in spirit and truth look like on an ordinary weekday?

deep.text: When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into the deep, and let down your nets for a catch.”
deep.question: Where is Jesus asking you to let down the net one more time?

deep.text: Deep calls to deep at the noise of your waterfalls. All your waves and your billows have swept over me.
deep.question: What deep in you is calling out to God today?

wisdom.text: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
wisdom.question: What decision in front of you needs to begin with reverence?

wisdom.text: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach; and it will be given to him.
wisdom.question: What wisdom do you need to ask for, plainly, today?

prayer.text: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.
prayer.question: What worry could you turn into a request right now?

prayer.text: Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
prayer.question: What would you say if you believed he was this near?

remembrance.text: I will remember Yah’s deeds; for I will remember your wonders of old.
remembrance.question: Which of God’s past deeds do you most need to remember today?

remembrance.text: Praise Yahweh, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits;
remembrance.question: Name three benefits you would rather not forget.

light.text: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
light.question: Where does the darkness seem strongest, and what does this verse say about it?

light.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. The light has shined on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death.
light.question: Who do you know who is still waiting for light?

He also gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given out in Susa to destroy them, to show it to Esther, and to declare it to her, and to urge her to go in to the king to make supplication to him, and to make request before him for her people.

verses.t: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the royal offspring.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were slain, even him and his nurse, and put them in the bedroom; and they hid him from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
He was with her hidden in Yahweh’s house six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the captains over hundreds of the Carites and of the guard, and brought them to him into Yahweh’s house; and he made a covenant with them, and made a covenant with them in Yahweh’s house, and showed them the king’s son.
He commanded them, saying, “This is what you must do: a third of you, who come in on the Sabbath, shall be keepers of the watch of the king’s house;
a third of you shall be at the gate Sur; and a third of you at the gate behind the guard. So you shall keep the watch of the house, and be a barrier.

verses.t: His servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him. Now he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who was over the household in Tirzah;
and Zimri went in and struck him and killed him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
When he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, he attacked all the house of Baasha. He didn’t leave him a single one who urinates on a wall among his relatives or his friends.
Thus Zimri destroyed all the house of Baasha, according to Yahweh’s word which he spoke against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
for all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, which they sinned and with which they made Israel to sin, to provoke Yahweh, the God of Israel, to anger with their vanities.
Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

verses.t: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe (now she lived in Jerusalem in the second quarter); and they talked with her.
She said to them, “Yahweh the God of Israel says, ‘Tell the man who sent you to me,
“Yahweh says, ‘Behold, I will bring evil on this place and on its inhabitants, even all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read.

Because they have forsaken me and have burned incense to other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands, therefore my wrath shall be kindled against this place, and it will not be quenched.’”
But to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of Yahweh, tell him, “Yahweh the God of Israel says, ‘Concerning the words which you have heard,

because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before Yahweh when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its inhabitants, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and have torn your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you,’ says Yahweh.

answers.name: Jesus

answers.name: Aaron

answers.name: Joshua the high priest

answers.name: Jeremiah

answers.name: Eleazar

answers.name: Zadok

answers.name: Jehoiada

answers.name: Azariah

answers.name: Amaziah

answers.name: Eli

answers.name: Hilkiah

answers.name: Abiathar
answers.note: Escaped from Nob and served David.

answers.name: Ezra
answers.note: A priest and scribe descended from Aaron.

answers.name: Phinehas
answers.note: Aaron's grandson.

answers.name: Ahijah
answers.note: Wore the ephod in Saul's camp.

answers.name: Ithamar
answers.note: A son of Aaron, named with his brothers.

answers.name: Nadab
answers.note: Aaron's son, who offered unauthorized fire.

answers.name: Seraiah
answers.note: Chief priest when Jerusalem fell.

answers.name: Ahimelech

answers.name: Eliashib
answers.note: High priest who helped rebuild the Sheep Gate.

answers.name: Abihu
answers.note: Aaron's son, who offered unauthorized fire.

answers.name: Pashhur
answers.note: The priest who put Jeremiah in the stocks.

answers.name: Zacharias
answers.note: Father of John the Baptist, of the division of Abijah.

answers.name: Ananias
answers.note: High priest at Paul's hearing.

answers.name: Urijah
answers.note: Priest in the days of Ahaz.

answers.name: Zephaniah
answers.note: The second priest when Jerusalem fell.

answers.name: Caiaphas
answers.note: High priest at the trial of Jesus.

answers.name: Jethro
answers.note: Priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law.

answers.name: Hophni
answers.note: Son of Eli.

answers.name: Annas
answers.note: High priest and father-in-law of Caiaphas.

answers.name: Mattan
answers.note: Priest of Baal.

answers.name: Potiphera
answers.note: Priest of On and Joseph's father-in-law.

answers.name: Ezekiel
answers.note: Called Ezekiel the priest.

answers.name: Sceva
answers.note: A Jewish chief priest whose seven sons are mentioned at Ephesus.

answers.name: Melchizedek
answers.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High.
answers.fact: Melchizedek, king of Salem, was priest of God Most High in the days of Abram (Genesis 14:18).

verses.t: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.

nearMisses.name: Samuel
nearMisses.message: He served at Shiloh and offered sacrifices, but Scripture calls him a prophet and judge, never a priest.

nearMisses.name: David
nearMisses.message: A king who worshipped and offered sacrifices, but not a priest.

nearMisses.name: Levi
nearMisses.message: The priestly tribe is named for him, but he lived long before the priesthood was given to Aaron's line.

nearMisses.name: Paul
nearMisses.message: An apostle; the New Testament does not call him a priest.

nearMisses.name: Potiphar
nearMisses.message: An easy mix-up: Potiphar was the captain of the guard (Genesis 39:1); Potiphera was the priest of On.

prompts.prompt: Name a person who built, rebuilt, or repaired an altar to the LORD in Scripture.

answers.name: Israel
answers.note: Built altars at Shechem and Bethel.

answers.name: David
answers.note: Built on the threshing floor he bought from Araunah.

answers.name: Moses
answers.note: Named one altar, The LORD is my Banner.

answers.name: Abraham
answers.note: Built altars at Shechem, Bethel, Hebron, and Moriah.

answers.name: Solomon
answers.note: Made the great bronze altar of the temple.

answers.name: Joshua
answers.note: Built on Mount Ebal of uncut stones.

answers.name: Manasseh
answers.note: Restored the altar of the LORD after his repentance.

answers.name: Isaac
answers.note: Built an altar at Beersheba.

answers.name: Samuel
answers.note: Built an altar at his home in Ramah.

answers.name: Elijah
answers.note: Repaired the altar on Carmel with twelve stones.

answers.name: Asa
answers.note: Renewed the altar before the temple porch.

answers.name: Noah
answers.note: The first altar named in Scripture, built after the flood.

answers.name: Gideon
answers.note: Called his altar, The LORD is Peace.

answers.name: Jeshua
answers.note: The priest who rebuilt the altar with Zerubbabel.

answers.name: Zerubbabel
answers.note: Rebuilt the altar on its site after the exile.

answers.name: Bezalel
answers.note: Made the altar of burnt offering for the tabernacle.

answers.name: Saul
answers.note: The first altar he built to the LORD.
answers.fact: The altar Saul built after the battle at Michmash was the first altar he built to the LORD (1 Samuel 14:35).

verses.t: Saul built an altar to Yahweh. This was the first altar that he built to Yahweh.

nearMisses.name: Cain
nearMisses.message: They brought offerings (Genesis 4:3–4), but no altar is mentioned; Noah's is the first.

nearMisses.name: Aaron
nearMisses.message: He built an altar at Sinai, but it stood before the golden calf (Exodus 32:5).

nearMisses.name: Balaam
nearMisses.message: Balak built seven altars at Balaam's word (Numbers 23:1), but in an attempt to curse Israel.

nearMisses.name: Ahaz
nearMisses.message: Uriah built an altar for Ahaz, copied from one in Damascus (2 Kings 16:10–11).

nearMisses.name: Jeroboam
nearMisses.message: He built an altar at Bethel for his own feast (1 Kings 12:32–33).

nearMisses.name: Reubenites
nearMisses.message: Their altar by the Jordan was a witness, not for offerings (Joshua 22:26–27).

nearMisses.name: Manoah
nearMisses.message: He offered on a rock (Judges 13:19), but is not said to have built an altar.

prompts.prompt: Name a woman of New Testament times who is named in the New Testament.

answers.name: Mary
answers.note: The mother of Jesus.

answers.name: Martha
answers.note: Sister of Mary and Lazarus.

answers.name: Mary Magdalene
answers.note: The first to see the risen Jesus in John's Gospel.

answers.name: Elizabeth
answers.note: Mother of John the Baptist.

answers.name: Herodias
answers.note: Wife of Herod Antipas.

answers.name: Anna
answers.note: A prophetess who saw the infant Jesus in the temple.

answers.name: Priscilla
answers.note: With Aquila, taught Apollos more accurately.

answers.name: Bernice
answers.note: Came with Agrippa to hear Paul.

answers.name: Dorcas
answers.note: A disciple at Joppa, raised to life through Peter.

answers.name: Joanna
answers.note: Wife of Chuzas, Herod's steward.

answers.name: Lydia
answers.note: A seller of purple, baptized at Philippi.

answers.name: Salome
answers.note: A follower of Jesus who went to the tomb.

answers.name: Apphia
answers.note: Greeted at the head of Philemon.

answers.name: Candace
answers.note: Queen of the Ethiopians; the name was probably a royal title.

answers.name: Chloe
answers.note: Her people brought Paul news from Corinth.

answers.name: Claudia
answers.note: Sends greetings to Timothy.

answers.name: Damaris
answers.note: Believed at Athens.

answers.name: Drusilla
answers.note: Wife of the governor Felix.

answers.name: Eunice
answers.note: Timothy's mother.

answers.name: Euodia
answers.note: A worker in the gospel at Philippi.

answers.name: Julia
answers.note: Greeted among the saints at Rome.

answers.name: Junia
answers.note: A relative of Paul and fellow prisoner; some translations read Junias.

answers.name: Lois
answers.note: Timothy's grandmother.

answers.name: Mary the mother of James and Joses
answers.note: Watched the crucifixion and saw the tomb.

answers.name: Mary the wife of Clopas
answers.note: Stood by the cross.

answers.name: Persis
answers.note: Worked hard in the Lord.

answers.name: Phoebe
answers.note: A servant of the church at Cenchreae.

answers.name: Sapphira
answers.note: Wife of Ananias.

answers.name: Susanna
answers.note: One of the women who provided for Jesus and the Twelve.

answers.name: Syntyche
answers.note: A worker in the gospel at Philippi.

answers.name: Tryphaena
answers.note: A worker in the Lord at Rome.

answers.name: Tryphosa
answers.note: A worker in the Lord at Rome.

answers.name: Mary of Bethany
answers.note: Anointed Jesus' feet.

answers.name: Mary the mother of John Mark
answers.note: The church met to pray in her house.

answers.name: Rhoda
answers.note: The servant girl who left Peter standing at the gate.
answers.fact: Rhoda was so glad to hear Peter at the gate that she ran in without opening it (Acts 12:13–14).

verses.t: When Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy, but ran in and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.
They said to her, “You are crazy!” But she insisted that it was so. They said, “It is his angel.”

nearMisses.name: Eve
nearMisses.message: Named in the New Testament, but she lived in Old Testament times.

nearMisses.name: Jezebel
nearMisses.message: Revelation 2:20 uses the name for a woman at Thyatira, probably as a symbol recalling Ahab's queen.

nearMisses.name: Veronica
nearMisses.message: From later tradition; she is not named in the New Testament.

nearMisses.name: Pilate's wife
nearMisses.message: She is in the Gospel (Matthew 27:19), but unnamed; the name comes from later tradition.

nearMisses.name: Samaritan woman
nearMisses.message: One of the best-known women in the Gospels, but John never gives her name (John 4:7).

nearMisses.name: Salome daughter of Herodias
nearMisses.message: Herodias's daughter danced for Herod (Mark 6:22), but the Gospels do not name her; the Salome named in Mark is a disciple.

prompts.prompt: Name a companion, co-worker, or host of Paul named in Acts or his letters.

answers.name: Mark
answers.note: Left the first journey, yet Paul later called him useful.

answers.name: Barnabas
answers.note: Set apart with Paul for the first journey.

answers.name: Timothy
answers.note: Joined Paul at Lystra and is named in many of his letters.

answers.name: Silas
answers.note: Travelled with Paul and sang with him in the Philippian jail.

answers.name: Titus
answers.note: Left in Crete to set things in order.

answers.name: Apollos
answers.note: An eloquent teacher from Alexandria.

answers.name: Aquila
answers.note: A tentmaker from Pontus who worked alongside Paul.

answers.name: Priscilla
answers.note: A tentmaker who, with her husband, hosted and worked with Paul.

answers.name: Aristarchus
answers.note: A Macedonian who sailed with Paul toward Rome.

answers.name: Gaius
answers.note: Host to Paul and to the whole church.

answers.name: Jason
answers.note: Paul's host in Thessalonica.

answers.name: Tychicus
answers.note: Carried Paul's letters and news.

answers.name: Demas
answers.note: A fellow worker who later left Paul.

answers.name: Epaphras
answers.note: Brought the gospel to Colossae.

answers.name: Erastus
answers.note: Sent ahead into Macedonia with Timothy.

answers.name: Justus
answers.note: A fellow worker who was a comfort to Paul.

answers.name: Luke
answers.note: The beloved physician; the only one with Paul at the end.

answers.name: Lydia
answers.note: A seller of purple who opened her home in Philippi.

answers.name: Stephanas
answers.note: His household were the first converts in Achaia.

answers.name: Trophimus
answers.note: An Ephesian whom Paul left sick at Miletus.

answers.name: Archippus
answers.note: Called a fellow soldier.

answers.name: Onesimus
answers.note: Sent back to Philemon as a beloved brother.

answers.name: Onesiphorus
answers.note: Often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chains.

answers.name: Publius
answers.note: The chief man of Malta, who hosted Paul three days.

answers.name: Sosthenes
answers.note: Named with Paul at the head of 1 Corinthians.

answers.name: Achaicus
answers.note: Visited Paul from Corinth.

answers.name: Andronicus
answers.note: A kinsman and fellow prisoner.

answers.name: Artemas
answers.note: Paul planned to send him to Crete.

answers.name: Carpus
answers.note: Paul left his cloak with him at Troas.

answers.name: Clement
answers.note: A fellow worker at Philippi.

answers.name: Crescens
answers.note: Went to Galatia.

answers.name: Euodia
answers.note: Laboured with Paul in the gospel.

answers.name: Fortunatus
answers.note: Visited Paul from Corinth.

answers.name: Junia
answers.note: A relative and fellow prisoner; some translations read Junias.

answers.name: Mnason
answers.note: An early disciple from Cyprus who lodged Paul.

answers.name: Philemon
answers.note: Paul asked him to prepare a guest room.

answers.name: Phoebe
answers.note: A servant of the church at Cenchreae and a helper of many.

answers.name: Secundus
answers.note: A Thessalonian who travelled with Paul.

answers.name: Sopater
answers.note: Of Beroea; travelled with Paul.

answers.name: Syntyche
answers.note: Laboured with Paul in the gospel.

answers.name: Tertius
answers.note: The scribe who wrote down Romans.

answers.name: Urbanus
answers.note: Called a fellow worker in Christ.

answers.name: Zenas
answers.note: The lawyer.

answers.name: Epaphroditus
answers.note: Carried the Philippians' gift and nearly died in the work.
answers.fact: Epaphroditus nearly died for the work of Christ while bringing the gift of the Philippians to Paul (Philippians 2:25–30).

verses.t: But I thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, fellow worker, fellow soldier, and your apostle and servant of my need,
since he longed for you all, and was very troubled because you had heard that he was sick.
For indeed he was sick nearly to death, but God had mercy on him, and not on him only, but on me also, that I might not have sorrow on sorrow.
I have sent him therefore the more diligently, that when you see him again, you may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.
Receive him therefore in the Lord with all joy, and hold such people in honor,
because for the work of Christ he came near to death, risking his life to supply that which was lacking in your service toward me.

nearMisses.name: Peter
nearMisses.message: A fellow apostle whom Paul once opposed at Antioch (Galatians 2:11), not a travelling companion.

nearMisses.name: Ananias
nearMisses.message: He laid hands on Paul in Damascus (Acts 9:17–18), but is not shown working alongside him.

nearMisses.name: Gamaliel
nearMisses.message: Paul's teacher before his conversion (Acts 22:3).

nearMisses.name: Stephen
nearMisses.message: Paul was present at Stephen's death, on the other side (Acts 7:58).

nearMisses.name: Alexander
nearMisses.message: Alexander the coppersmith did Paul much harm (2 Timothy 4:14).

answers.name: Sosthenes

answers.name: Archelaus

answers.name: Lysanias

answers.name: Sergius Paulus

answers.name: Tiberius

verses.t: Gaius, my host and host of the whole assembly, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, as does Quartus, the brother.

nearMisses.name: Nero

nearMisses.name: Ethiopian eunuch
nearMisses.message: A high official indeed (Acts 8:27), but Luke does not give his name.

nearMisses.name: Julius Caesar
nearMisses.message: He died in 44 BC and is not named in the New Testament.

nearMisses.name: Zacchaeus
nearMisses.message: A tax collector rather than a ruler or governor.

nearMisses.name: David
nearMisses.message: A king, but of the Old Testament era.

prompts.prompt: Name a title or name given to Jesus in the New Testament.

answers.name: Lord
answers.note: Every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.

answers.name: God
answers.note: Thomas's confession on seeing the risen Jesus.

answers.name: King of the Jews
answers.note: Sought by the wise men; written above the cross.

answers.name: The Way, the Truth, and the Life
answers.note: No one comes to the Father except through him.

answers.name: The Word
answers.note: The Word became flesh and lived among us.

answers.name: I AM
answers.note: Before Abraham came into existence, I AM.

answers.name: High Priest
answers.note: He has passed through the heavens.

answers.name: Christ

answers.name: Head of the Church

answers.name: Prophet

answers.name: Bread of Life

answers.name: Cornerstone

answers.name: Light of the World

answers.name: The Door

answers.name: Son of Man

answers.name: Lamb of God

answers.name: Image of the invisible God

answers.name: Lion of Judah

answers.name: Firstborn

answers.name: Good Shepherd

answers.name: Rabbi

answers.name: Apostle

answers.name: The Amen
answers.note: The faithful and true witness.

answers.name: True Vine

answers.name: Holy One of God
answers.note: Recognized even by an unclean spirit.

answers.name: Root of David
answers.note: Both David's root and David's offspring.

answers.name: Son of God
answers.note: Mark's Gospel opens with it.

answers.name: Savior
answers.note: Announced by the angel to the shepherds.

answers.name: Resurrection and the Life

answers.name: Son of David
answers.note: The crowd's cry as he entered Jerusalem.

answers.name: Bridegroom
answers.note: His answer to a question about fasting.

answers.name: Shepherd and Overseer of souls

answers.name: Alpha and Omega
answers.note: The first and the last.

answers.name: Righteous One

answers.name: King of kings

answers.note: The name written on his robe.

answers.name: Nazarene
answers.note: From the town where he grew up.

answers.name: Mediator

answers.name: Only begotten Son

answers.name: Faithful witness

answers.name: Morning Star

answers.name: Immanuel

answers.name: Advocate
answers.note: He speaks to the Father for us.

answers.name: Lord of glory
answers.note: The one the rulers of this age crucified.

answers.name: Author and perfecter of faith
aliases: Author and finisher of our faith

answers.name: Chief Shepherd
answers.note: He will give the unfading crown of glory.

answers.name: Great Shepherd
answers.note: Brought again from the dead.

answers.name: Last Adam
answers.note: A life-giving spirit.

answers.name: Prince of life
answers.note: Peter's words in Solomon's porch.

answers.name: Dayspring
answers.note: From Zacharias's song.
answers.fact: Zacharias sang that the dayspring from on high had visited his people (Luke 1:78).

verses.t: because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the dawn from on high will visit us,

nearMisses.name: Prince of Peace
nearMisses.message: From Isaiah 9:6, which Christians read of Christ, but the title itself is not repeated in the New Testament.

nearMisses.name: Redeemer

nearMisses.name: Rose of Sharon
nearMisses.message: From Song of Solomon 2:1; applied to Christ in hymns, not in the New Testament.

nearMisses.name: Jehovah
nearMisses.message: The divine name in the Old Testament; the New Testament writes Lord.

nearMisses.name: Man of Sorrows
nearMisses.message: From Isaiah 53, which the New Testament applies to Jesus, but the title itself is not repeated there.

answers.name: Romans

answers.name: Ephesians

answers.name: Galatians

answers.name: Hebrews

answers.name: James

answers.name: Philippians
answers.note: A letter of joy written in chains.

answers.name: 1 John

answers.name: 1 Peter
answers.note: Written to believers scattered through five provinces.

answers.name: 1 Timothy

answers.name: 2 Corinthians
answers.note: Paul learns that grace is sufficient in weakness.

answers.name: Colossians

answers.name: 1 Thessalonians

answers.name: 2 Peter

answers.name: 2 Thessalonians

answers.name: 2 Timothy

answers.name: 3 John

answers.name: Jude

answers.name: Philemon

answers.name: Titus

answers.name: 2 John

prompts.prompt: Name a parable or miracle of Jesus.

answers.fact: Jesus sent Peter, a fisherman, to cast a hook and find the temple tax in the mouth of the first fish he caught (Matthew 17:27).

verses.t: When they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma coins came to Peter, and said, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the didrachma?”

He said, “Yes.” When he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From their children, or from strangers?”
Peter said to him, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Therefore the children are exempt.

But, lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take that, and give it to them for me and you.”

nearMisses.message: That covers many miracles. Which one do you have in mind?

answers.name: Jecoliah

answers.name: Jehoaddin
answers.note: The mother of King Amaziah.

answers.name: Jehosheba
answers.note: Hid the infant Joash from Athaliah.

answers.name: Jerusha
answers.note: The mother of King Jotham.

answers.name: Lo-ruhamah
answers.note: Hosea's daughter; her name means not pitied.

answers.name: Noadiah
answers.note: A prophetess who tried to frighten Nehemiah.

answers.name: Peninnah
answers.note: Elkanah's other wife, who provoked Hannah.

answers.name: Shimeath
answers.note: An Ammonite woman whose son killed King Joash.

answers.name: Tahpenes
answers.note: A queen of Egypt.

answers.name: Zibiah
answers.note: The mother of King Joash.

answers.name: Apphia
answers.note: Greeted at the head of the letter to Philemon.

answers.name: Atarah
answers.note: A wife of Jerahmeel.

answers.name: Baara
answers.note: A wife of Shaharaim.

answers.name: Bithiah
answers.note: Pharaoh's daughter, married to Mered.

answers.name: Candace
answers.note: Queen of the Ethiopians.

answers.name: Chloe
answers.note: Her household brought Paul news from Corinth.

answers.name: Claudia
answers.note: Sends greetings to Timothy.

answers.name: Damaris
answers.note: A woman of Athens who believed.

answers.name: Drusilla
answers.note: The wife of the governor Felix.

answers.name: Elisheba
answers.note: Aaron's wife.

answers.name: Euodia
answers.note: A worker in the gospel at Philippi.

answers.name: Hammoleketh
answers.note: A sister of Gilead.

answers.name: Hazzelelponi
answers.note: A sister in the line of Judah.

answers.name: Hodesh
answers.note: A wife of Shaharaim.

answers.name: Iscah
answers.note: The daughter of Haran.

answers.name: Jedidah
answers.note: The mother of King Josiah.

answers.name: Jemimah
answers.note: Job's first daughter after his restoration.

answers.name: Jerioth
answers.note: A wife of Caleb.

answers.name: Judith
answers.note: A wife of Esau, daughter of Beeri the Hittite.

answers.name: Julia
answers.note: Greeted among the saints at Rome.

answers.name: Junia
answers.note: A relative of Paul and a fellow prisoner.

answers.name: Keren-happuch
answers.note: Job's third daughter after his restoration.

answers.name: Keziah
answers.note: Job's second daughter after his restoration.

answers.name: Meshullemeth
answers.note: The mother of King Amon.

answers.name: Nehushta
answers.note: The mother of King Jehoiachin.

answers.name: Persis
answers.note: She worked hard in the Lord.

answers.name: Reumah
answers.note: Nahor's concubine.

answers.name: Sheerah
answers.note: She built the two Beth Horons.

answers.name: Shimrith
answers.note: A Moabite woman whose son killed King Joash.

answers.name: Shiphrah
answers.note: A Hebrew midwife who feared God and spared the boys.

answers.name: Susanna
answers.note: One of the women who provided for Jesus from their means.

answers.name: Syntyche
answers.note: A worker in the gospel at Philippi.

answers.name: Taphath
answers.note: A daughter of Solomon.

answers.name: Tryphaena
answers.note: A worker in the Lord at Rome.

answers.name: Tryphosa
answers.note: A worker in the Lord at Rome.

answers.name: Zebidah
answers.note: The mother of King Jehoiakim.

answers.name: Zeruah
answers.note: The mother of Jeroboam.

answers.name: Noah
answers.note: A daughter of Zelophehad.
answers.fact: Noah was also a woman's name: she and her four sisters asked Moses for their father's inheritance and received it (Numbers 27:1–7).

verses.t: Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

Then the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph came near. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

nearMisses.name: Lot's wife
nearMisses.message: She looked back and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26), but Scripture never gives her name.

nearMisses.name: Potiphar's wife
nearMisses.message: She is in Genesis 39:7, but the text never gives her name.

nearMisses.name: Noah's wife
nearMisses.message: She went into the ark (Genesis 7:13), but Genesis never names her.

nearMisses.name: Job's wife
nearMisses.message: She speaks in Job 2:9, but is never named.

nearMisses.name: Samaritan woman
nearMisses.message: One of the best-known women in the Gospels, but John never gives her name (John 4:7).

nearMisses.name: Veronica
nearMisses.message: A name from later tradition. The Gospels do not name a Veronica.

nearMisses.name: Queen of Sheba
nearMisses.message: She visited Solomon (1 Kings 10:1), but Scripture gives her title, not her name.

nearMisses.name: Pilate's wife
nearMisses.message: She sent Pilate a warning (Matthew 27:19), but the Gospel does not name her.

nearMisses.name: Mary Magdalene the prostitute
nearMisses.message: Scripture says seven demons had gone out of Mary Magdalene (Luke 8:2). It never calls her a prostitute.

nearMisses.name: Oholah
nearMisses.message: Ezekiel's names for Samaria and Jerusalem in a parable (Ezekiel 23:4), not women who lived.

nearMisses.name: Lilith
nearMisses.message: Not a woman in Scripture. Isaiah 34:14 has a word some translations render "night creature".

prompts.prompt: Name a person raised from the dead in the Bible.

answers.name: Jesus
answers.note: "He is not here, for he has risen."

answers.name: Lazarus
answers.note: Called out of the tomb after four days.

answers.name: Jairus' daughter
answers.note: "Little girl, I tell you, get up!" She was twelve.

answers.name: Tabitha
answers.note: A disciple at Joppa, full of good works; Peter said, "Tabitha, get up!"

answers.name: Shunammite woman's son
answers.note: Elisha stretched himself on the child, who sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

answers.name: Eutychus
answers.note: Fell from a third-story window while Paul preached late; he was taken up dead and brought back alive.

answers.name: Widow of Nain's son
aliases: son of the widow of Nain
answers.note: Jesus touched the bier, and the young man sat up and began to speak.

answers.name: Saints who came out of the tombs
answers.note: At Jesus' death the tombs were opened, and many saints were raised.

answers.name: Two witnesses
answers.note: In John's vision, the breath of life from God entered them after three and a half days.

answers.name: Widow of Zarephath's son
aliases: son of the widow of Zarephath
answers.note: Elijah cried to the LORD, and the child's life came back into him.

answers.name: Man thrown into Elisha's grave
answers.note: Thrown into Elisha's tomb in a hurry, he touched Elisha's bones and stood up.
answers.fact: He is the only person in Scripture raised by touching a dead prophet's bones: he revived and stood up when his body touched Elisha's (2 Kings 13:21).

verses.t: Elisha died, and they buried him. Now the bands of the Moabites invaded the land at the coming in of the year.
As they were burying a man, behold, they saw a band of raiders; and they threw the man into Elisha’s tomb. As soon as the man touched Elisha’s bones, he revived, and stood up on his feet.

nearMisses.name: Widow's son
nearMisses.message: Two widows' sons were raised: at Zarephath through Elijah (1 Kings 17:22) and at Nain by Jesus (Luke 7:15). Name the town and cast again.

nearMisses.name: Elijah
nearMisses.message: Elijah never died: he went up to heaven in a whirlwind (2 Kings 2:11).

nearMisses.name: Enoch
nearMisses.message: Enoch never died: "he was not found, because God took him" (Genesis 5:24; Hebrews 11:5).

nearMisses.name: Samuel
nearMisses.message: At Endor the medium saw Samuel come up (1 Samuel 28:11–14), but he was not raised to life again.

prompts.prompt: Name a person in the Bible who was given a new name or also went by another name.

answers.name: Jacob
answers.note: Renamed after he wrestled through the night at Peniel.

answers.name: Abraham
answers.note: "Your name will no more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham."

answers.name: Peter
answers.note: Jesus said, "You shall be called Cephas," which means Peter.

answers.name: Paul
answers.note: Known first as Saul of Tarsus.
answers.fact: There is no renaming scene on the Damascus road: Acts 13:9 simply says "Saul, who is also called Paul," and Luke uses Paul from then on.

answers.name: Daniel
answers.note: The chief of the eunuchs gave him a Babylonian name.

answers.name: Sarah
answers.note: Renamed when God promised she would be a mother of nations.

answers.name: Esther
answers.note: Mordecai's cousin, also called Hadassah.

answers.name: Solomon
answers.note: The LORD sent word through Nathan to name him Jedidiah, "beloved of the LORD."

answers.name: Joseph
answers.note: Pharaoh gave him an Egyptian name when he made him ruler over Egypt.

answers.name: Joshua
answers.note: Moses called Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua.

answers.name: Esau
answers.note: Called Edom, "red," after the red stew.

answers.name: Abednego
answers.note: One of Daniel's three friends.

answers.name: Gideon
answers.note: Called Jerubbaal after he tore down Baal's altar.

answers.name: Shadrach
answers.note: One of Daniel's three friends.

answers.name: Meshach
answers.note: One of Daniel's three friends.

answers.name: Naomi
answers.note: "Don't call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me."

answers.name: Benjamin
answers.note: Rachel named him Ben-oni as she died; Jacob called him Benjamin.

answers.name: Zedekiah
answers.note: The king of Babylon renamed the last king of Judah.

answers.name: Mark
answers.note: "John who was called Mark."

answers.name: Jehoiakim
answers.note: Pharaoh Necho made Eliakim king and renamed him.

answers.name: Barnabas
answers.note: The apostles called Joses Barnabas, Son of Encouragement.

answers.name: Jehoiachin
answers.note: Jeremiah calls him Coniah; Chronicles and Matthew call him Jeconiah.

answers.name: Reuel
answers.note: Moses' father-in-law, the priest of Midian, is called Reuel and Jethro.

answers.name: James and John
answers.note: Jesus called the brothers Boanerges, Sons of Thunder.

answers.name: Thomas
answers.note: "Thomas, who is called Didymus," the Twin.

answers.name: Barsabbas
answers.note: "Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also called Justus," put forward to replace Judas.

answers.name: Tabitha
answers.note: A disciple at Joppa; both names mean gazelle.

answers.name: Thaddaeus
answers.note: "Lebbaeus, who was also called Thaddaeus," one of the Twelve.

answers.name: Niger
answers.note: One of the prophets and teachers at Antioch.

answers.name: Pashhur
answers.note: The priest who put Jeremiah in the stocks.
answers.fact: Jeremiah told him the LORD had renamed him Magor-missabib, "terror on every side," because he would become a terror to himself and his friends (Jeremiah 20:3–4).

verses.t: Now Pashhur, the son of Immer the priest, who was chief officer in Yahweh’s house, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things.
Then Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks that were in the upper gate of Benjamin, which was in Yahweh’s house.
On the next day, Pashhur released Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then Jeremiah said to him, “Yahweh has not called your name Pashhur, but Magormissabib.

nearMisses.name: Levi
nearMisses.message: Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27 call the tax collector Levi, and Matthew 9:9 tells the same call with the name Matthew, but no verse says he was "also called," so he isn't counted here.

nearMisses.name: Nathanael
nearMisses.message: Nathanael (John 1:45) and Bartholomew (Matthew 10:3) are never said in the text to be the same man.

nearMisses.name: Immanuel
nearMisses.message: Immanuel is a title given to Jesus (Matthew 1:23); try titles of Jesus in another round.

prompts.prompt: Name one of Jesus' "I am" sayings in John.

answers.name: Light of the world
answers.note: "He who follows me will not walk in the darkness."

answers.name: Bread of life
answers.note: "He who comes to me will not be hungry."

answers.name: Way, the truth, and the life
answers.note: "No one comes to the Father, except through me."

answers.name: Good shepherd
answers.note: "The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep."

answers.name: True vine
answers.note: "I am the vine. You are the branches."

answers.name: Resurrection and the life
answers.note: Said to Martha before he raised Lazarus.

answers.name: Door
answers.note: "If anyone enters in by me, he will be saved."

answers.name: Before Abraham was, I am
answers.note: Said in the temple; the crowd took up stones to throw at him.
answers.fact: It is the one "I am" saying with no picture attached: "Before Abraham came into existence, I AM" (John 8:58), and the crowd picked up stones (8:59).

verses.t: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, before Abraham came into existence, I AM.”

nearMisses.name: Life
nearMisses.message: Three sayings use it: the bread of life (6:35), the resurrection and the life (11:25), and the way, the truth, and the life (14:6). Name one.

nearMisses.name: Alpha and Omega
nearMisses.message: "I am the Alpha and the Omega" is in Revelation (1:8; 22:13), not in John's Gospel.

nearMisses.name: Lamb of God
nearMisses.message: John the Baptist called Jesus the Lamb of God (John 1:29); Jesus doesn't say it of himself.

prompts.prompt: Name something Jesus said from the cross.

answers.name: It is finished
answers.note: His last word in John's Gospel before he gave up his spirit.

answers.name: Father, forgive them
answers.note: "Father, forgive them, for they don't know what they are doing."

answers.name: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me
answers.note: Words of Psalm 22:1, cried out about the ninth hour.

answers.name: Today you will be with me in Paradise
answers.note: Said to one of the criminals crucified with him.

answers.name: I thirst
answers.note: Said "that the Scripture might be fulfilled"; they gave him sour wine on hyssop.

answers.name: Father, into your hands I commit my spirit
answers.note: Words of Psalm 31:5, his last words in Luke.

answers.name: Woman, behold your son
answers.note: Said to his mother and to the disciple whom he loved.
answers.fact: With these words he entrusted his mother to the disciple whom he loved, who took her into his own home from that hour (John 19:26–27).

verses.t: Therefore when Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing there, he said to his mother, “Woman, behold, your son!”
Then he said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother!” From that hour, the disciple took her to his own home.

nearMisses.name: Remember me
aliases: remember me when you come into your kingdom
nearMisses.message: Those were the words of the criminal beside him (Luke 23:42); Jesus answered, "Today you will be with me in Paradise."

nearMisses.name: Not my will
nearMisses.message: That was his prayer in Gethsemane the night before (Luke 22:42), not from the cross.

nearMisses.name: Truly this was the Son of God
nearMisses.message: The centurion said that when Jesus died (Matthew 27:54).

prompts.prompt: Name a giant, or a people of giants, in the Bible.

answers.name: Goliath
answers.note: The champion of Gath, six cubits and a span tall.

answers.name: Nephilim
answers.note: "The Nephilim were on the earth in those days."

answers.name: Og
answers.note: King of Bashan, the last of the Rephaim.
answers.fact: Og's iron bedstead was nine cubits long and four wide, and Moses notes it could still be seen in Rabbah of the Ammonites (Deuteronomy 3:11).

answers.name: Anakim
answers.note: The spies felt like grasshoppers beside them.

answers.name: Rephaim
answers.note: An ancient people counted as giants, of whom Og was the last.

answers.name: Arba
answers.note: The greatest man among the Anakim; Hebron was once called Kiriath Arba after him.

answers.name: Anak
answers.note: The ancestor of the Anakim, after whom his sons were named.

answers.name: Egyptian
answers.note: A man five cubits tall with a spear like a weaver's beam; Benaiah took it from him.

answers.name: Talmai
answers.note: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron.

answers.name: Ahiman
answers.note: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron.

answers.name: Emim
answers.note: Moab's name for the giants who once lived in its land.

answers.name: Sheshai
answers.note: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron.

answers.name: Saph
answers.note: Of the sons of the giant, killed by Sibbecai.

answers.name: Lahmi
answers.note: Goliath's brother, killed by Elhanan.

answers.name: Six fingers
answers.note: Six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot; killed by Jonathan, David's nephew.

answers.name: Zamzummim
answers.note: The Ammonites' name for the giants who once lived in their land.

answers.name: Ishbi-benob
answers.note: Of the sons of the giant; he set out to kill David.
answers.fact: His bronze spear weighed three hundred shekels, and he nearly killed a weary David before Abishai struck him down (2 Samuel 21:16–17).

verses.t: and Ishbibenob, who was of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear was three hundred shekels of bronze in weight, he being armed with a new sword, thought he would kill David.

But Abishai the son of Zeruiah helped him, and struck the Philistine and killed him. Then the men of David swore to him, saying, “Don’t go out with us to battle any more, so that you don’t quench the lamp of Israel.”

nearMisses.name: Giant
nearMisses.message: Name one. (Where the KJV says "giants" in Genesis 6:4, the WEB says Nephilim.)

nearMisses.name: Samson
nearMisses.message: Samson was strong, but the Bible never calls him a giant (Judges 16).

nearMisses.name: Saul
nearMisses.message: Saul stood head and shoulders above everyone (1 Samuel 9:2), but he isn't called a giant.

prompts.prompt: Name one of the ten plagues of Egypt.

answers.name: Blood
answers.note: The water of the Nile turned to blood, and the fish died.

answers.name: Frogs
answers.note: Frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.

answers.name: Darkness
answers.note: Three days of darkness that could be felt; Israel had light.

answers.name: Death of the firstborn
answers.note: At midnight; the Passover blood marked Israel's doors.

answers.name: Locusts
answers.note: An east wind brought them, and they ate every green thing.

answers.name: Hail
answers.note: Fire ran along the ground with the hail.

answers.name: Flies
answers.note: Swarms filled Egypt but not the land of Goshen.

answers.name: Boils
answers.note: Ashes from a furnace became boils on people and animals.

answers.name: Lice
answers.note: The dust of the earth became lice; the magicians said, "This is God's finger."

answers.name: Death of livestock
answers.note: A severe pestilence on Egypt's livestock in the field.
answers.fact: The KJV calls it "a very grievous murrain"; Pharaoh sent to check, and not one of Israel's animals had died (Exodus 9:3–7).

verses.t: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, ‘This is what Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go, that they may serve me.
For if you refuse to let them go, and hold them still,
behold, Yahweh’s hand is on your livestock which are in the field, on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the herds, and on the flocks with a very grievous pestilence.
Yahweh will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt; and nothing shall die of all that belongs to the children of Israel.”’”
Yahweh appointed a set time, saying, “Tomorrow Yahweh shall do this thing in the land.”
Yahweh did that thing on the next day; and all the livestock of Egypt died, but of the livestock of the children of Israel, not one died.

nearMisses.name: Serpent
nearMisses.message: Aaron's staff becoming a serpent was a sign before Pharaoh (Exodus 7:10), not one of the ten plagues.

nearMisses.name: Red Sea
nearMisses.message: The Red Sea crossing came after the plagues, when Israel had left Egypt (Exodus 14).

prompts.prompt: Name a fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23).

answers.name: Peace
answers.note: Third in Paul's list.

answers.name: Love
answers.note: First in Paul's list.

answers.name: Joy
answers.note: "The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace…"

answers.name: Kindness
answers.note: The WEB's kindness is the KJV's gentleness in verse 22.

answers.name: Patience
answers.note: The KJV reads longsuffering.

answers.name: Faith
answers.note: Both the WEB and the KJV read faith here; many modern versions say faithfulness.

answers.name: Gentleness
answers.note: The WEB's gentleness (verse 23) is the KJV's meekness; the KJV's "gentleness" is in verse 22, so either way it counts.

answers.name: Self-control
answers.note: Last in the list; the KJV reads temperance.

answers.name: Goodness
answers.note: Sixth in the list.
answers.fact: Goodness is the one fruit Paul names again in Ephesians: "the fruit of the Spirit is in all goodness and righteousness and truth" (Ephesians 5:9).

verses.t: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,

nearMisses.name: Hope
nearMisses.message: Hope abides with faith and love (1 Corinthians 13:13), but it isn't in the Galatians list.

nearMisses.name: Grace
nearMisses.message: A good gift, but not one of the nine in Galatians 5:22–23.

prompts.prompt: Name a piece of the armor of God (Ephesians 6:14–17).

answers.name: Sword of the Spirit
answers.note: "Which is the word of God."

answers.name: Shield of faith
answers.note: It quenches all the fiery darts of the evil one.

answers.name: Helmet of salvation
answers.note: Isaiah 59:17 pictures God himself wearing it.

answers.name: Breastplate of righteousness
answers.note: Also in Isaiah 59:17 and 1 Thessalonians 5:8.

answers.name: Belt of truth
answers.note: Truth buckled around the waist.

answers.name: Shoes of the gospel of peace
answers.note: Feet fitted with the preparation of the Good News of peace.
answers.fact: Neither the WEB nor the KJV actually says "shoes" here: the feet are "shod" (KJV) or "fitted" (WEB) "with the preparation of the gospel of peace" (Ephesians 6:15).

verses.t: and having fitted your feet with the preparation of the Good News of peace,

nearMisses.name: Prayer
nearMisses.message: Prayer follows the list in Ephesians 6:18, but Paul doesn't make it a piece of armor.

nearMisses.name: Spear
nearMisses.message: Not in Paul's list of the armor of God (Ephesians 6:14–17).

prompts.prompt: Name one of the seven churches of Revelation.

answers.name: Ephesus
answers.note: The church that had left its first love.

answers.name: Laodicea
answers.note: Neither hot nor cold, but lukewarm.

answers.name: Philadelphia
answers.note: Given an open door that no one can shut.

answers.name: Sardis
answers.note: "You have a reputation of being alive, but you are dead."

answers.name: Smyrna
answers.note: "Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life."

answers.name: Pergamum
answers.note: "Where Satan's throne is"; the KJV spells it Pergamos.

answers.name: Thyatira
answers.note: Praised for its love and service, warned about "Jezebel."
answers.fact: Lydia, the seller of purple whom Paul met at Philippi, came from Thyatira (Acts 16:14).

verses.t: saying, “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.”
“To the angel of the assembly in Thyatira write: “The Son of God, who has his eyes like a flame of fire, and his feet are like burnished brass, says these things:
“I know your works, your love, faith, service, patient endurance, and that your last works are more than the first.

But I have this against you, that you tolerate your woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess. She teaches and seduces my servants to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to repent of her sexual immorality.
Behold, I will throw her and those who commit adultery with her into a bed of great oppression, unless they repent of her works.

nearMisses.name: Colossae
nearMisses.message: Paul's letters or travels went there, but it isn't one of the seven churches of Revelation 2–3.

prompts.prompt: Name a city of refuge.

answers.name: Hebron
answers.note: In the hill country of Judah.

answers.name: Shechem
answers.note: In the hill country of Ephraim.

answers.name: Ramoth
answers.note: East of the Jordan, for the tribe of Gad.

answers.name: Kedesh
answers.note: In Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali.

answers.name: Golan
answers.note: East of the Jordan, in Bashan, for Manasseh.

answers.name: Bezer
answers.note: In the wilderness, on the plain, for Reuben.
answers.fact: Bezer was one of the three refuge cities Moses set apart east of the Jordan before Israel crossed (Deuteronomy 4:41–43).

verses.t: Beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness in the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

nearMisses.name: Jerusalem
nearMisses.message: Not one of the six cities of refuge (Joshua 20:7–8).

prompts.prompt: Name someone a psalm's title credits.

answers.name: David
answers.note: Named in the titles of more psalms than anyone else.

answers.name: Moses
answers.note: "A Prayer by Moses, the man of God."

answers.name: Solomon
answers.note: Two psalms are credited to him.

answers.name: Asaph
answers.note: Psalm 50 and Psalms 73–83.

answers.name: Korah
answers.note: Credited with eleven psalms, including "As the deer pants."

answers.name: Heman
answers.note: Psalm 88, the darkest of the psalms.

answers.name: Ethan
answers.note: Psalm 89, on God's covenant with David.
answers.fact: Ethan the Ezrahite was so famous for wisdom that Solomon's is measured against him: Solomon "was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite" (1 Kings 4:31).

verses.t: A contemplation by Ethan, the Ezrahite. I will sing of the loving kindness of Yahweh forever. With my mouth, I will make known your faithfulness to all generations.

nearMisses.name: Jeduthun
nearMisses.message: Jeduthun is named in the titles of Psalms 39, 62 and 77 as a musician, not as the writer.

nearMisses.name: Chief musician
nearMisses.message: The "chief musician" in many titles is a musician, not a named writer.

prompts.prompt: Name a person, thing, or place in the Garden of Eden account (Genesis 2–3).

answers.name: Eve
answers.note: "She will be called 'woman'"; Adam named her Eve, mother of all living.

answers.name: Serpent
answers.note: "More subtle than any animal of the field."

answers.name: Adam
answers.note: Formed from the dust of the ground.

answers.name: Tree of the knowledge of good and evil
answers.note: The one tree whose fruit they were not to eat.

answers.name: God
answers.note: Planted the garden and walked in it in the cool of the day.

answers.name: Fruit
answers.note: She saw that it was good for food and pleasant to the eyes.

answers.name: Fig leaves
answers.note: Sewn together to cover themselves.

answers.name: Tree of life
answers.note: Guarded after they were sent out of the garden.

answers.name: Rib
answers.note: Taken from Adam while he slept, to make the woman.

answers.name: Livestock
answers.note: Brought to the man to see what he would call them.

answers.name: Flaming sword
answers.note: "A flaming sword which turned every way."

answers.name: River
answers.note: A river went out of Eden and parted into four heads.

answers.name: Dust
answers.note: "For you are dust, and to dust you shall return."

answers.name: Cherubim
answers.note: Placed at the east of the garden to guard the way.

answers.name: Thorns
answers.note: The ground would bring them out after the curse.

answers.name: Euphrates
answers.note: The fourth river.

answers.name: Gold
answers.note: "The gold of that land is good."

answers.name: Assyria
answers.note: The Tigris flows east of it.

answers.name: Deep sleep
answers.note: God caused it to fall on the man.

answers.name: Breath of life
answers.note: Breathed into the man's nostrils.

answers.name: Cush
answers.note: The Gihon flows around it; the KJV says Ethiopia.

answers.name: Garments of skins
answers.note: God made them and clothed Adam and Eve.

answers.name: Heel
answers.note: "He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel."

answers.name: Onyx
answers.note: Found in Havilah.

answers.name: Havilah
answers.note: A land of gold.

answers.name: Gihon
answers.note: The second river, flowing around Cush.

answers.name: Thistles
answers.note: "Thorns also and thistles it will bring out to you."

answers.name: Mist
answers.note: Went up from the earth and watered the ground.

answers.name: Sweat
answers.note: "By the sweat of your face you will eat bread."

answers.name: Hiddekel
answers.note: The third river, the Tigris; both the WEB and the KJV say Hiddekel.

answers.name: Pishon
answers.note: The first river, flowing around Havilah.

answers.name: Bdellium
answers.note: Found in Havilah with gold and onyx.
answers.fact: Bdellium appears once more in Scripture: manna looked like it (Numbers 11:7).

verses.t: and the gold of that land is good. Bdellium and onyx stone are also there.

nearMisses.name: Apple
nearMisses.message: Genesis never names the fruit of that tree (Genesis 3:6).

nearMisses.name: Lucifer
nearMisses.message: Genesis 3 says "the serpent"; Revelation 12:9 later calls the devil "the old serpent." Try "serpent."

nearMisses.name: Eden
nearMisses.message: That's the setting. Name something in it.

prompts.prompt: Name something that came down from heaven or the sky in the Bible.

answers.name: Fire
answers.note: Fire from the LORD consumed Elijah's sacrifice on Carmel.

answers.name: Dove
answers.note: The Spirit descended on Jesus at his baptism.

answers.name: Manna
answers.note: Bread rained from heaven for forty years.

answers.name: Angel
answers.note: An angel came down and rolled away the stone.

answers.name: Rain
answers.note: The windows of heaven opened for forty days and nights.

answers.name: Hail
answers.note: The seventh plague, and the great hail of Revelation 16.

answers.name: Brimstone
answers.note: Rained on Sodom and Gomorrah.

answers.name: Jesus
answers.note: "I have come down from heaven."

answers.name: Voice
answers.note: "This is my beloved Son."

answers.name: Tongues of fire
answers.note: A sound from heaven like a rushing wind at Pentecost.

answers.name: New Jerusalem
answers.note: Coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride.

answers.name: Sheet
answers.note: Let down by its four corners, full of animals, in Peter's vision.

answers.name: Light
answers.note: A light from the sky shone around Saul near Damascus.

answers.name: Satan
answers.note: "I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven."

answers.name: Stars
answers.note: The stars fell to the earth like unripe figs.

answers.name: Dew
answers.note: The dew of heaven, part of Isaac's blessing.

answers.name: Snow
answers.note: "As the rain comes down and the snow from the sky."

answers.name: Wormwood
answers.note: A great star burning like a torch, making the waters bitter.

answers.name: Great stones
answers.note: Hurled down on the Amorites fleeing Gibeon.
answers.fact: More of the Amorites died from the stones that fell from the sky than the Israelites killed with the sword (Joshua 10:11).

verses.t: As they fled from before Israel, while they were at the descent of Beth Horon, Yahweh hurled down great stones from the sky on them to Azekah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel killed with the sword.

nearMisses.name: Chariot of fire
nearMisses.message: Elijah's chariot went up, not down (2 Kings 2:11).

nearMisses.name: Quail
nearMisses.message: The quail were brought by a wind from the sea (Numbers 11:31), not said to fall from heaven.

nearMisses.name: Ladder
nearMisses.message: The ladder stood on the earth with its top reaching heaven (Genesis 28:12); try the angels on it.

prompts.prompt: Name something Jesus says the kingdom of heaven (or of God) is like.

answers.name: Mustard seed
answers.note: The smallest of seeds grows into a tree.

answers.name: Treasure hidden in a field
answers.note: A man sold all he had to buy that field.

answers.name: Yeast
answers.note: Hidden in three measures of meal until all was leavened.

answers.name: Pearl
answers.note: He sold everything to buy one pearl of great price.

answers.name: Net
answers.note: Cast into the sea, gathering fish of every kind.

answers.name: Wedding feast
answers.note: A king made a wedding feast for his son.

answers.name: Ten virgins
answers.note: Five were wise and took oil for their lamps.

answers.name: Wheat and tares
answers.note: An enemy sowed weeds among the wheat.

answers.name: King settling accounts
answers.note: Forgiven a huge debt, the servant would not forgive a small one.

answers.name: Seed growing by itself
answers.note: The seed sprouts and grows; the sower doesn't know how.

answers.name: Laborers in the vineyard
answers.note: The last were paid the same as the first.

answers.name: Talents
answers.note: Servants entrusted with talents while their master was away.

answers.name: Householder
answers.note: Brings out of his treasure things new and old.
answers.fact: Jesus says every scribe instructed in the kingdom of heaven is like a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old (Matthew 13:52).

verses.t: He said to them, “Therefore every scribe who has been made a disciple in the Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who is a householder, who brings out of his treasure new and old things.”

nearMisses.name: Sower
nearMisses.message: The sower explains "the word of the Kingdom" (Matthew 13:19), but Jesus doesn't open it with "the kingdom is like."

nearMisses.name: Little child
nearMisses.message: Jesus says the kingdom belongs to such as these (Matthew 19:14), not that it is like them.

prompts.prompt: Name a creature, figure, or object in the book of Revelation.

answers.name: Beast
answers.note: One beast rises from the sea and another from the earth.

answers.name: Lamb
answers.note: Standing as though it had been slain, in the midst of the throne.

answers.name: Mark of the beast
answers.note: Received on the right hand or on the forehead.

answers.name: Dragon
answers.note: A great red dragon with seven heads and ten horns, called the old serpent.

answers.name: Six hundred sixty-six
answers.note: "His number is six hundred sixty-six."

answers.name: Babylon
answers.note: "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great."

answers.name: Seven seals
answers.note: A scroll sealed with seven seals that only the Lamb could open.

answers.name: Satan
answers.note: Thrown down to the earth.

answers.name: Twenty-four elders
answers.note: Seated on thrones, casting their crowns before the throne.

answers.name: Throne
answers.note: One sat on it, and a rainbow was around it.

answers.name: John
answers.note: "I, John, your brother."

answers.name: Seven trumpets
answers.note: Given to the seven angels who stand before God.

answers.name: Four living creatures
answers.note: Full of eyes, crying "Holy, holy, holy."

answers.name: New Jerusalem
answers.note: Coming down out of heaven from God.

answers.name: White horse
answers.note: Its rider "came forth conquering, and to conquer."

answers.name: Alpha and Omega
answers.note: The beginning and the end.

answers.name: Lake of fire
answers.note: The second death.

answers.name: One hundred forty-four thousand
aliases: hundred and forty and four thousand
answers.note: Sealed from every tribe of Israel.

answers.name: Armageddon
answers.note: Where the kings of the whole world are gathered.

answers.name: Pale horse
answers.note: Its rider's name was Death.

answers.name: Patmos
answers.note: The island where John received the revelation.

answers.name: Death
answers.note: Death rode the pale horse, and Hades followed.

answers.name: Bride
answers.note: The Lamb's wife, made ready.

answers.name: Street of gold
answers.note: Pure gold, like transparent glass.

answers.name: Woman clothed with the sun
answers.note: With the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars.

answers.name: Great multitude
answers.note: From every nation, tribe, people and language, which no one could count.

answers.name: River of the water of life
answers.note: Clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.

answers.name: Lion of the tribe of Judah
answers.note: "The Root of David has overcome."

answers.name: Prostitute
answers.note: She sits on many waters.

answers.name: Seven bowls
answers.note: Full of the wrath of God; the KJV says vials.

answers.name: Seven stars
answers.note: Held in his right hand: the angels of the seven churches.

answers.name: Two witnesses
answers.note: They prophesy for 1,260 days, clothed in sackcloth.

answers.name: Locusts
answers.note: Out of the smoke of the abyss, shaped like horses prepared for war.

answers.name: Michael
answers.note: He and his angels made war on the dragon.

answers.name: False prophet
answers.note: Thrown into the lake of fire with the beast.

answers.name: Tree of life
answers.note: Bearing twelve kinds of fruit, its leaves for the healing of the nations.

answers.name: Abyss
answers.note: The beast comes up out of it; Satan is shut in it.

answers.name: Gates of pearl
answers.note: Each gate was made of a single pearl.

answers.name: Seven golden lamp stands
answers.note: The seven churches.

answers.name: Book of life
answers.note: Whoever was not found written in it was cast into the lake of fire.

answers.name: Thousand years
answers.note: Satan is bound, and they reign with Christ.

answers.name: King of kings
answers.note: Written on his garment and on his thigh.

answers.name: Rainbow
answers.note: Around the throne, like an emerald to look at.

answers.name: Black horse
answers.note: Its rider held a balance in his hand.

answers.name: Red horse
answers.note: Its rider was given power to take peace from the earth.

answers.name: Sea of glass
answers.note: Before the throne, like crystal.

answers.name: Golden altar
answers.note: Where an angel offered incense with the prayers of the saints.

answers.name: Ark of the covenant
answers.note: Seen in God's temple in heaven.

answers.name: Son of Man
answers.note: Among the lampstands, with eyes like a flame of fire.

answers.name: Incense
answers.note: The prayers of the saints.

answers.name: Balaam
answers.note: His teaching was held by some at Pergamum.

answers.name: Reed
answers.note: A measuring reed, used for the temple and later the city.

answers.name: Eagle
answers.note: Flying in mid heaven, crying "Woe, woe, woe."

answers.name: Euphrates
answers.note: Dried up to prepare the way for the kings from the east.

answers.name: Jezebel
answers.note: The self-styled prophetess at Thyatira.

answers.name: Censer
answers.note: Filled with fire from the altar and thrown to the earth.

answers.name: Hidden manna
answers.note: Promised to the one who overcomes at Pergamum.

answers.name: Winepress
answers.note: The great winepress of the wrath of God.

answers.name: Frogs
answers.note: Three unclean spirits like frogs.

answers.name: Gog
answers.note: The nations gathered for battle at the end of the thousand years.

answers.name: Sickle
answers.note: The harvest of the earth.

answers.name: Key
answers.note: The keys of Death and of Hades.

answers.name: Jasper
answers.note: The city's light was like a jasper stone.

answers.name: Abaddon
answers.note: The angel of the abyss, their king.

answers.name: Faithful and True
answers.note: The rider on the white horse.

answers.name: Little book
answers.note: Sweet as honey in John's mouth, bitter in his stomach.

answers.name: Morning star
answers.note: "I am the root and the offspring of David, the bright and morning star."

answers.name: Key of David
answers.note: He opens and no one can shut.

answers.name: Marriage supper
answers.note: "Blessed are those who are invited."

answers.name: Nicolaitans
answers.note: Their works the church at Ephesus hated.

answers.name: Antipas
answers.note: "My faithful witness, who was killed among you."

answers.name: White stone
answers.note: With a new name written on it that no one knows.

answers.name: Wormwood
answers.note: A great star, burning like a torch, fell on the rivers and springs.
answers.fact: When the star called Wormwood fell, a third of the waters became wormwood, and many people died from the bitter water (Revelation 8:11).

verses.t: The third angel sounded, and a great star fell from the sky, burning like a torch, and it fell on one third of the rivers, and on the springs of water.
The name of the star is “Wormwood.” One third of the waters became wormwood. Many people died from the waters, because they were made bitter.

nearMisses.name: Antichrist
nearMisses.message: The word "antichrist" is in 1 and 2 John (1 John 2:18; 2 John 7), not in Revelation.

nearMisses.name: Rapture
nearMisses.message: "Rapture" is not a word used in Revelation.

nearMisses.name: Four horses
nearMisses.message: Name a rider or a horse: white, red, black, or pale (Revelation 6).

prompts.prompt: Name a person put in prison, a pit, a cistern, or a den in the Bible.

answers.name: Joseph
answers.note: Thrown into a pit by his brothers, then into Pharaoh's prison.

answers.name: Paul
answers.note: Prayed and sang in the Philippi jail at midnight.

answers.name: Daniel
answers.note: Thrown into the lions' den; God shut the lions' mouths.

answers.name: Peter
answers.note: Led out of prison by an angel the night before his trial.

answers.name: Jeremiah
answers.note: Let down by ropes into a muddy cistern.

answers.name: John
answers.note: Herod put him in prison for speaking about Herodias.

answers.name: Silas
answers.note: Sang hymns with Paul in the stocks at Philippi.

answers.name: Barabbas
answers.note: In prison for insurrection and murder; released instead of Jesus.

answers.name: Apostles
answers.note: An angel opened the prison doors by night.

answers.name: Samson
answers.note: Blinded and set to grind grain in the prison at Gaza.

answers.name: Cupbearer
answers.note: Joseph interpreted his dream in prison.

answers.name: Baker
answers.note: Joseph interpreted his dream too, with a darker ending.

answers.name: Zedekiah
answers.note: Blinded and kept in prison in Babylon until he died.

answers.name: Simeon
answers.note: Kept bound in Egypt until his brothers brought Benjamin.

answers.name: Micaiah
answers.note: Fed "bread of affliction" in prison for prophesying against Ahab.

answers.name: Hoshea
answers.note: The last king of Israel, imprisoned by the king of Assyria.

answers.name: Jehoiachin
answers.note: Released from prison after thirty-seven years and given a seat at the king's table.

answers.name: Aristarchus
answers.note: Paul's "fellow prisoner."

answers.name: Epaphras
answers.note: "My fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus."

answers.name: Andronicus
answers.note: Paul's relative and fellow prisoner.

answers.name: Junia
answers.note: Paul's relative and fellow prisoner, with Andronicus.

answers.name: Hanani
answers.note: The seer who rebuked King Asa.
answers.fact: When Hanani rebuked Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of the LORD, the king put him in the prison house in a rage (2 Chronicles 16:10).

verses.t: At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah, and said to him, “Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and have not relied on Yahweh your God, therefore the army of the king of Syria has escaped out of your hand.
Weren’t the Ethiopians and the Lubim a huge army, with chariots and exceedingly many horsemen? Yet, because you relied on Yahweh, he delivered them into your hand.

For Yahweh’s eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. You have done foolishly in this; for from now on you will have wars.”
Then Asa was angry with the seer, and put him in the prison; for he was in a rage with him because of this thing. Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time.

nearMisses.name: Shadrach
nearMisses.message: They were thrown into a fiery furnace (Daniel 3), not a prison.

nearMisses.name: Jonah
nearMisses.message: Jonah was swallowed by a great fish (Jonah 1:17), not imprisoned.

prompts.prompt: Name a person the Bible says wept or cried.

answers.name: David
answers.note: "O my son Absalom!"

answers.name: Peter
answers.note: He went out and wept bitterly after denying Jesus.

answers.name: Jesus
answers.note: "Jesus wept."
answers.fact: "Jesus wept" (John 11:35) is the shortest verse in most English Bibles, but Jesus also wept over Jerusalem (Luke 19:41) and with loud cries and tears (Hebrews 5:7).

answers.name: Jacob
answers.note: He kissed Rachel and wept.

answers.name: Joseph
answers.note: He wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard.

answers.name: Mary Magdalene
answers.note: She stood outside the tomb weeping.

answers.name: Hannah
answers.note: She wept and would not eat, praying for a son.

answers.name: Abraham
answers.note: Came to mourn and weep for Sarah.

answers.name: Jeremiah
answers.note: "Oh that my head were waters, and my eyes a spring of tears."

answers.name: Hezekiah
answers.note: Wept bitterly when told he would die.

answers.name: Esau
answers.note: "Bless me, even me also, my father!"

answers.name: Ruth
answers.note: They lifted up their voices and wept.

answers.name: Hagar
answers.note: She sat apart so she would not watch the child die.

answers.name: Nehemiah
answers.note: Sat down and wept when he heard Jerusalem's walls were broken.

answers.name: Moses
answers.note: Pharaoh's daughter opened the basket, and the baby cried.

answers.name: Saul
answers.note: Lifted up his voice and wept when David spared him.

answers.name: Elders of Ephesus
answers.note: They all wept and fell on Paul's neck.

answers.name: Benjamin
answers.note: Wept on Joseph's neck.

answers.name: Paul
answers.note: He warned the Ephesians night and day with tears.

answers.name: John
answers.note: Wept much because no one was worthy to open the scroll.

answers.name: Jonathan
answers.note: He and David kissed one another and wept.

answers.name: Elisha
answers.note: Wept over the harm Hazael would do to Israel.

answers.name: Job
answers.note: "My face is red with weeping."

answers.name: Josiah
answers.note: He tore his clothes and wept when the Law was read.

answers.name: Esther
answers.note: Fell at the king's feet and begged him with tears.

answers.name: Rachel
answers.note: "Rachel weeping for her children."

answers.name: Tamar
answers.note: Went away crying aloud.

answers.name: Ezra
answers.note: Weeping and casting himself down before the house of God.

answers.name: Widows
answers.note: Stood weeping and showing the garments Dorcas had made.

answers.name: Timothy
answers.note: Paul remembered his tears.

answers.name: Naomi
answers.note: Wept with her daughters-in-law on the road to Judah.

answers.name: Orpah
answers.note: She kissed Naomi goodbye.

answers.name: Joash
answers.note: The king of Israel wept over Elisha in his last illness.
answers.fact: King Joash wept over the dying Elisha and cried, "My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" (2 Kings 13:14), the words Elisha had once cried over Elijah.

verses.t: Now Elisha became sick with the illness of which he died; and Joash the king of Israel came down to him, and wept over him, and said, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”

nearMisses.name: Jesus wept
nearMisses.message: Just the name: Jesus. (The verse is John 11:35.)

prompts.prompt: Name a person the Bible says ran.

answers.name: David

answers.name: Peter

answers.name: Zacchaeus

answers.name: Father

answers.name: Abraham

answers.name: Esau
answers.note: Ran to meet Jacob and embraced him.

answers.name: Mary Magdalene
answers.note: Ran to tell Peter that the stone had been taken away.

answers.name: Women
answers.note: Ran to bring the disciples word.

answers.name: Samuel
answers.note: Ran to Eli: "Here I am; for you called me."

answers.name: Philip
answers.note: Ran to the Ethiopian's chariot.

answers.name: Rebekah
answers.note: Ran to draw water for all the camels.

answers.name: Disciple whom Jesus loved
answers.note: Outran Peter to the tomb.

answers.name: Rhoda
answers.note: Ran in to say Peter was at the gate, and forgot to open it.

answers.name: Aaron
answers.note: Ran into the assembly with incense as the plague began.

answers.name: Elisha
answers.note: Left the oxen and ran after Elijah.

answers.name: Laban
answers.note: Ran out to the man at the spring.

answers.name: Asahel
answers.note: "As light of foot as a wild gazelle."

answers.name: Ahimaaz
answers.note: Outran the Cushite to bring David news.

answers.name: Gehazi
answers.note: Ran after Naaman to take a gift.

answers.name: Cushite
answers.note: Sent to tell David of the battle.

answers.name: Elijah
answers.note: Ran ahead of Ahab's chariot to Jezreel.
answers.fact: With the hand of the LORD on him, Elijah tucked up his cloak and ran ahead of Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel (1 Kings 18:46).

verses.t: Yahweh’s hand was on Elijah; and he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.

nearMisses.name: Jonah
nearMisses.message: Jonah fled toward Tarshish by ship (Jonah 1:3); the text doesn't say he ran.

prompts.prompt: Name a person or group the Bible says fasted.

answers.name: Jesus
answers.note: Fasted forty days and forty nights in the wilderness.

answers.name: Moses
answers.note: Forty days on the mountain without bread or water.

answers.name: Esther
answers.note: "Fast for me… I and my maidens will also fast."

answers.name: David
answers.note: Fasted and lay on the ground while his child was sick.

answers.name: Daniel
answers.note: Sought the Lord with prayer and fasting, sackcloth and ashes.

answers.name: Nineveh
answers.note: Believed God and proclaimed a fast.

answers.name: Israelites
answers.note: Fasted at Bethel and at Mizpah.

answers.name: Paul
answers.note: "In fastings often."

answers.name: Ezra
answers.note: Proclaimed a fast at the river Ahava.

answers.name: Nehemiah
answers.note: Fasted and prayed when he heard of Jerusalem.

answers.name: Anna
answers.note: Served God with fastings and prayers night and day.

answers.name: Jews
answers.note: Great mourning, fasting and weeping in every province.

answers.name: Pharisee

So he made the pillars; and there were two rows of pomegranates around the one network, to cover the capitals that were on the top of the pillars; and he did so for the other capital.
The capitals that were on the top of the pillars in the porch were of lily work, four cubits.
There were capitals above also on the two pillars, close by the belly which was beside the network. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows around the other capital.

verses.t: The donkey saw Yahweh’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the donkey turned out of the path, and went into the field. Balaam struck the donkey, to turn her into the path.
Then Yahweh’s angel stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.
The donkey saw Yahweh’s angel, and she thrust herself to the wall, and crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall. He struck her again.
Yahweh’s angel went further, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.
The donkey saw Yahweh’s angel, and she lay down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burned, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Yahweh opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
